meta.schemaNotes: Value format. Every number that enters the model is an object {value, p10, p90, source, tier} with optional note and rule. value is the point value (the median of the prior), p10 and p90 the 10th and 90th percentiles. tier: 'observed' = computed from measured or reported data of Singapore buildings or households (BCA records, SingStat surveys, EMA statistics, field studies); 'published_table' = read from a code, standard or official table (BCA codes, Green Mark, NEA labels, SS 553 as reproduced by NEA, ISO 13790 classes); 'assumed' = judgement, or a derivation with at least one assumed input (rule says which). source names ids of meta.sources with table or page. Non-numeric fields (holidays, T_heat null, natCtrl, systemPrior) carry {value or shares, source, tier}. Units. U W/(m²K); g, frameFrac, WWR, coolFrac, RH_cool, equipBase 0–1; Cm J/(m²K) per m² of reference area; n50, n_vent, n_nat 1/h; floorHeight m floor to floor; T °C; start, end, acStart, acEnd local hours (UTC+8, end exclusive; acStart > acEnd wraps past midnight); daysPerWeek counted from Monday; Q_int, Q_lat, P_light, P_equip W/m²; hPart W/K per m²; E_other, dhw kWh/(m²a); COP_cool W/W (COP = 3.517 / kW/RT); E_common kWh per dwelling and year. Reference area. Every W/m² and kWh/(m²a) value is per m² of the type's areaBasis. Non-residential: GFA (the basis of BCA EUI, car parks generally excluded); GFA = refAreaFactor × footprint × storeys. rc5 uses Af = 0.85 × footprint × storeys, so a value per Af = value per GFA × refAreaFactor / 0.85 (or × BCA GFA / Af where bca.json has the building). Residential: the dwelling floor area (HDB: resale floor_area_sqm; condo: strata area). For an HDB block, Σ flat area = Σ x.hdb.units × households.byDwelling.<type>.floorArea (flatAreaByLeaseDecade refines it by era, flatAreaPublished gives HDB's own plan areas); else refAreaFactor × footprint × storeys above the void deck. rc5's residential Af comes from the GEG volume rule, so a value per Af = value × Σ flat area / Af. rc5.js keys (header of 2026-11-25). - Q_int: occupant sensible gain only (P_light and P_equip are always given). Residential: 24-h mean at all hours. Non-residential: mean during start–end, 0 outside (the Green Mark schedule shares are folded in). - Q_lat: residential = 24-h mean latent gain of the dwelling (people, cooking, bathing) per m² of reference area, as rc5 asks; rc5 counts it in the cooled share while the AC runs. Non-residential = latent gain during use per m² of cooled area (people sit in the cooled rooms). Q_int_acZone and Q_lat_acZone (households.byDwelling) give the sleepers' gains per m² of cooled bedroom during the AC hours, for information; rc5 does not read them. - P_light, P_equip: non-residential means during use, equipBase × P_equip outside; residential 24-h means. - coolFrac: share of the reference area cooled while the AC runs. Residential coolFrac = acOwnership × acUseShare × 0.8 (bedrooms cooled) × bedroomShare (households.byDwelling); the HDB type value is the stock mix, recompute per block. - acStart, acEnd: residential night AC hours (sample them independently within p10–p90). Non-residential = start, end. - hPart: W/K per m² of floor of the smaller zone; natCtrl: 0 windows open whenever AC is off, 1 only when outdoor air is cooler; binary, sample 1 with probability pOne. - n_vent: residential = air change of a closed AC bedroom on top of infiltration 0.07 × n50. Non-residential = V_oa / 3 m. - n_nat: windows open (residential when the AC is off; non-residential uncooled share). T_heat null: no heating. hr_eff 0. - COP_cool: systems.<key>.COP_cool; systems.<key>.scope says what it covers. Central plants (chw_water, chw_air) are the total system (TSE): chillers, pumps, cooling towers AND air-side fans, so AHU/FCU fans are NOT in P_equip or E_other. COP_plant is given for a model that books the fans elsewhere. Unitary units: whole unit incl. fans. District cooling (dcs): air side only, the building meter. Choose the key from bca.json "Type of AC System" via meta.systemKeyMap, else draw it from types.<type>.systemPrior.shares, else types.<type>.defaultSystem. - E_other: annual electricity not modelled hourly. HDB E_other is the flat only. HDB common property (lifts, corridor and stair lighting, booster pumps) is paid by the Town Councils and is NOT in EMA household electricity: types.hdb.commonProperty.E_common (kWh per dwelling and year) is for a building total and must not be added when comparing with EMA household data. Condo common property (MCST) likewise. - dhw (non-residential): useful heat for information; its electric part is inside E_other. Eras. types.hdb.eras: pick by HDB completion year (x.hdb.year), merge era.params over types.hdb.params. condo.eras by TOP year. Non-residential: pick nrEras by TOP year (bca.json TOP/CSC year), start from nrEnvelope[era], then apply types.<type>.params (the type wins: e.g. industrial U_roof), then types.<type>.WWR_byEra if present (office). Variants (healthcare clinic, nursingHome; education ihl) merge over the type params; defaultVariant names the default. Validation data (households.byDwelling.*.electricityEMA_kWhPerMonth) are targets, never inputs. The residential P_light, P_equip and E_other are anchored on EMA 2017 national means, so residential validation must use other years (e.g. 2019, 2022–2025) and should look at the spatial and dwelling-type pattern. BCA EUI entered only office E_other (lifts and other 15 % of the 2025 median office EUI, BCA_SLE shares) and nothing else; the AC floor share, system type and kW/RT of BCA_BEBRDATA are building attributes, not EUI.

gaps: HDB U-values, glazing g and window-to-wall ratios: no HDB specification beyond "tinted glass" and component thicknesses; walls and roofs derived from BCA k-values, g and WWR assumed.
Air tightness (n50) of any Singapore dwelling or commercial building: none found (one tracer-gas office study, values only in a figure); all n50 assumed, wide.
Window-open natural ventilation rate (n_nat) in HDB flats: no measurement found; assumed 10 (3–30) h⁻¹.
AC hours and set points by household: only secondary citations of paywalled surveys (Chua & Chou 2010; Yang & Olofsson 2017) and one NEA statistic (54 % set ≥ 25 °C).
Field COP of residential split units in Singapore: none found; rated values × field factor 0.8 (0.6–1.0).
Number of AC units per household, water heater types, cooking fuel shares: not collected by HES; town gas use per account exists (EMA), shares not official.
HDB common-property electricity per block (lifts, lighting, pumps): not published; derived from one Town Council's spending with an assumed tariff.
SS 553:2016 outdoor-air table and SS 554 comfort table: paywalled; V_oa assumed.
Office/retail/hotel equipment loads: only design reference values (Green Mark) and a 15 % lighting share; operating values assumed.
Industrial process loads and MOE school AC share: no data; assumed with wide ranges.
Condominium and landed floor areas and constructions: no official statistic read; assumed.

retrofit._note: Retrofit measures of the Singapore page (js/retrofit_sg.js). Each measure sets one or more rc5 inputs to a target from a published source; the page applies it to the same parameter draws as the current state and reports the paired savings of electricity and CO₂ with P10-P90. A measure never makes an input worse: the new value is the better of the draw and the target (min for U_roof, g_window and P_light, max for COP_cool and T_cool). Tiers as in meta.tiers: 'published_table' when the target is read from a code or official table, 'assumed' when its derivation needs a judgement (rule says which). Left out because the model cannot express them or no source fixes them: a cool roof or cool facade paint (rc5 has no absorptance input; α 0.5 walls and 0.6 roof are fixed in js/rc5.js after ISO 13790 §11.3); internal blinds (shadeCtrl already stands for the curtains and blinds in use, and no published transmittance for Singapore blinds was read); LED lighting in flats (Green Mark lighting power budgets cover only the common areas of residential buildings, BCA_ETG2024 §12 p. 47, and common areas are not in the model).

Central plants: COP = 3.517 / TSE at the Green Mark Platinum level. District cooling: the building meter has the air side only.

window.rule: 5.50 × 0.8; the field factor is the assumed one of the stock rule

split.source: NEA_TICK (single-split and multi-split, 5 ticks: weighted COP ≥ 5.50); BCA_ESC4 RB02-1 p. 6 (5-tick split units required in new residential buildings); field factor 0.8 of systems.split.COP_cool.rule
split.rule: 5.50 × 0.8; the field factor is the assumed one of the stock rule

vrf.source: NEA_TICK (three-phase VRF, 5 ticks: IEER ≥ 6.15); field factor 0.75 of systems.vrf.COP_cool.rule
vrf.rule: 6.15 × 0.75; the field factor is the assumed one of the stock rule

unitary.source: mean of the split and vrf targets, as systems.unitary.COP_cool

plant.unit: kW/RT total system efficiency (TSE: chillers, pumps, cooling towers and air-side fans); COP = 3.517 / TSE

dcs.source: BCA_ETG2024 p. 10 (buildings on DCS, DDC or CCS: air-side efficiency in lieu of TSE; GoldPLUS 0.2, Platinum 0.18, SLE 0.16 kW/RT)

glazing.note: Solar control film or low-e glazing to the deemed-to-satisfy shading coefficient of the Code for Environmental Sustainability at the window-to-wall ratio of the draw (above 0.50, the last row). g = 0.87 × SC (SC is relative to 3 mm clear glass, BCA_ENV2008 Appendix B, PDF p. 21).

nonResidential.format: [WWR below (the last: up to and including), SC_glass at most]

residential.format: [WWR below (the last: up to and including), SC_glass at most]

roof.note: Roof insulation to the maximum average U-value of the Code for Environmental Sustainability for the roof weight group of the type.

residential.source: BCA_ESC4 RB01-2, Table 4.1(a), p. 5 (light < 50, medium 50–230, heavy > 230 kg/m²)

nonResidential.source: BCA_ESC4 NRB01-2(b), Table 4.1(b), p. 7 (roof without skylights)

hdb.source: HDB_BTO2024 ("Reinforced concrete roof slab with precast concrete secondary roofing")

landed.source: clay tiles over a ceiling or a reinforced concrete flat roof (types.landed U_roof note); medium taken

default.source: reinforced concrete roof slab assumed for the other non-residential types

lighting.note: LED lighting to the Green Mark Platinum lighting power budget (BCA_ETG2024 Table 2A, column B, pp. 47–49). The type value of P_light is a mean during use per m² GFA, derived from SS 530 budgets or installed values (types.<type>.params.P_light); the target repeats that derivation with the Platinum budget in its place and is stored as a ratio to the type value, so variants and blended mixed developments follow. The page sets P_light to min(draw, ratio × the building value). Not for flats: Green Mark budgets for residential buildings cover only common areas (BCA_ETG2024 §12, p. 47).

office.source: BCA_ETG2024 Table 2A p. 47 (Offices: Platinum 5.5 W/m²); BCA_EMG2024 Table 2 (lighting mean 0.875 over 07–19)
office.rule: the derivation of types.office P_light (installed about 8 W/m² × 0.875) with 5.5 W/m² installed: 0.875 × 5.5 = 4.81; ratio 4.81 / 7.0

retail.source: BCA_ETG2024 Table 2A p. 48 (Retail (General Lighting): Platinum 7, SS 530 15 W/m²)
retail.rule: the type value 14 stands for the SS 530 retail budgets (general 15, specialty 20–35, corridors 7); scaled by 7 / 15. Specialty shops (Platinum totals 11–19 W/m²) are not separated

hotel.source: BCA_ETG2024 Table 2A p. 48 (Hotel Guest Rooms: Platinum 7, SS 530 12 W/m²)
hotel.rule: the type value 4.0 is a 24-h mean of guest rooms (12), lobbies (10) and corridors (7) at SS 530; scaled by the guest-room ratio 7 / 12

mixed.source: the office and retail targets above, blended as types.mixed P_light
mixed.rule: 0.647 × 4.81 × 11/14 + 0.353 × 6.53, the weights that give the type value 8.5 from office 7 and retail 14

education.source: BCA_ETG2024 Table 2A p. 47 (Classrooms, Lecture Theatre: Platinum 5.5, SS 530 12 W/m²)
education.rule: the type values (school 6, IHL 8) stand for the SS 530 classroom budget with daylight use; scaled by 5.5 / 12

healthcare.source: BCA_ETG2024 Table 2A pp. 47–48 (Offices 5.5/12, Lobby 4.5/10, Toilets 5/10 W/m², Platinum/SS 530)
healthcare.rule: the type values stand for SS 530 budgets of 10–12 W/m²; scaled by the mean Platinum/SS 530 ratio of those rows, 0.46

industrial.source: BCA_ETG2024 Table 2A p. 49 (Manufacturing (general): Platinum 6.5, SS 530 13 W/m²)
industrial.rule: scaled by 6.5 / 13; warehouses (5 / 7) are not separated

other.source: BCA_ETG2024 Table 2A p. 48 (Multi Purpose Hall: Platinum 7, SS 530 16 W/m²)
other.rule: the type value stands for SS 530 hall budgets of 10–16 W/m²; scaled by 7 / 16

T_cool.source: MSE_GO25 (setting indoor air-conditioning at or above 25 °C, with alternatives such as fans); NEA_ACMV p. 162–163 (SS 553 design dry bulb 23–25 °C)

fans.unit: W per m² of air-conditioned floor while the AC runs
fans.source: NEA_HOME2016 p. 4 (install fans; ceiling fans are more effective than standing fans); fan power assumed
fans.rule: a 30 W ceiling fan per AC bedroom of 12.5 m² (the master bedroom of households.byDwelling.*.bedroomArea), counted only where the set point rises by 1 K or more (a smaller change is one step of the remote control); its heat is removed by the AC, so its electricity is × (1 + 1/COP). Non-residential: no fans, as 25 °C is within the SS 553 design range

shading.note: External horizontal shading over every window (overhangs or ledges), as the effective shading coefficient SC2 of the Envelope Code: g × SC2 (SC = SC1 × SC2, BCA_ENV2008 Appendix B2.1, p. 21). SC2 of each facade by its orientation, weighted by the solar irradiation on its windows in the model (after shading by the neighbours).

R1.source: assumed: a projection half the window height (for example 0.75 m over a 1.5 m window), no inclination

SC2.source: BCA_ENV2008 Table C12 p. 42 (North & South, R1 0.5, 0 °: 0.7210) and Table C13 p. 43 (East & West: 0.7248)
